summary: Soroako Airport is a small airfield located in the highlands of South Sulawesi, Indonesia, primarily serving the mining town of Soroako. The town is best known as the site of one of the world's largest nickel mining operations, run by PT Vale Indonesia. The airport's traffic is largely tied to the mining industry, with flights typically connecting to Makassar and other regional hubs.
faqs:
Q: Who primarily uses Soroako Airport?
A: The airport mainly serves employees and contractors of the local nickel mining operations, along with occasional visitors to the region.

Q: Are there commercial flights to Soroako?
A: Scheduled passenger flights are limited; most services operate on small turboprop aircraft and schedules can change frequently.

Q: Where can I fly to from Soroako?
A: Flights typically connect to Makassar (Hasanuddin International Airport), the main gateway for South Sulawesi.

Q: Are there facilities at the airport?
A: As a small airfield, amenities are minimal, so travelers should arrange any special needs in advance.
transport_tips: Ground transportation is usually arranged through mining company shuttles or pre-booked private vehicles, as public transport options are very limited. The airport is a short drive from Soroako town, but road conditions can be affected by weather and mining activity. Taxis are scarce, so confirming pickup arrangements before arrival is strongly recommended.
local_tip: If visiting for leisure, ask about boat trips on Lake Matano, one of the deepest lakes in the world and a stunning natural feature of the region that most business travelers miss.
